Key person cover puts liquidity on the balance sheet at the exact event — profit replaced, facilities covered, a replacement funded. That is the entire product, and RR Branch places it every week.

Structuring the cover

Term insures the event. Whole life insures the person leaving by any door

Top-up Term layerMatched to the recovery window and the bank facility. Cheap cover for a big number — and it expires when the exposure does.
Core Whole life layerPermanent, builds cash value the company owns, still in force at 70 to fund the shareholder buy-out — and an asset if the key person simply leaves.
+ Critical illness acceleration + Total & permanent disability Company proposes · pays · benefits

And the clause almost nobody writes: agree upfront what happens to the policy if they leave — surrender it, transfer it to them, or re-designate it to their successor. That one line is what makes the vehicle answer emigration, burnout and retirement.

Why most of it fails

Most “keyman” policies are just policies

Sold, not structured

  • A sum assured picked out of the air
  • No financials read, nothing quantified
  • Nothing a board or banker can act on
  • The business stays exposed — and nobody knows
